title: 3 Simple Strategies To Get Your Students To Pay Attention
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin offers three everyday, low-prep strategies for capturing student attention without relying on elaborate, attention-grabbing lesson openers that aren't sustainable for daily use. The first is a short pre-lesson exercise break to boost brain function and mood before instruction begins. The second is storytelling, used to introduce lesson content by giving abstract ideas emotional and narrative context that makes them easier to remember. The third is curiosity, structured as a promise to students that something interesting is coming if they stay engaged through the early part of a lesson, which creates active anticipation. He frames these as practical, repeatable tools rather than occasional showpieces, closing with an encouraging reminder that engaging strategies exist for even the most challenging teaching days.
points: Elaborate, attention-grabbing lesson openers aren't realistic for daily use; simple, repeatable tools are needed instead.
A brief pre-lesson exercise break boosts brain function, mood, and readiness to learn.
Storytelling gives abstract lesson content emotional and narrative context that improves attention and recall.
The curiosity strategy promises students a payoff later in the lesson, creating active anticipation that sustains engagement.
quotes: How do you get them to pay attention in a world of instant gratification?
Students love these kinds of things, no doubt about it. But every day? For every lesson? It just isn’t realistic.
Studies show that exercise can boost brain function, improve mood, and increase learning.
Storytelling is a powerful way to introduce lessons. Nothing captures attention as effectively.
Stories also provide deeply layered context for students, linking their memories, emotions, and viewpoints to your lesson objectives.
By holding back the part of the lesson that is most interesting or attractive to students, and dangling it like a carrot, you provide students a compelling reason to pay attention.
Shortcuts, strategies, and solutions abound to make teaching easier, faster, less stressful, more effective, and a lot more fun.
